pr.title: interpret: project_downcast: do not ICE for uninhabited variants
pr.description:
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120337

This assertion was already under discussion for a bit; I think the [example](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120337#issuecomment-1911076292) @tmiasko found is the final nail in the coffin. One could argue maybe MIR building should read the discriminant before projecting, but even then MIR optimizations should be allowed to remove that read, so the downcast should still not ICE. Maybe the downcast should be UB, but in this example UB already arises earlier when a value of type `E` is constructed.

r? @oli-obk
pr.author: RalfJung

processing.reason: The PR is a bug fix whose historical failure mode is an ICE (removed `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited())`) or missed const propagation (`return None` for a downcast to an uninhabited variant), not a defined value-changing miscompilation. The decoded GVN before/after diff is the *corrected* new behavior: it folds `((_2 as A).1: u32)` to `const 0_u32` only because the tested program already constructs/reads an uninhabited enum value through a union, which the PR itself calls UB. Thus there is no source-grounded, Miri-defined execution in which the historical original and the historically incorrect transformation produce different concrete values. Modeling the old rejection as a panic/ICE would not produce a defined value, and modeling it as an arbitrary numeric return would manufacture an unrelated rewrite forbidden by the task. The const-eval UI test and Miri test were added to check that such downcasts no longer ICE; they do not provide a defined original-vs-transformed value divergence.

analysis.originalLogic: In const evaluation's downcast projection, the code computed the variant layout and then required it to be inhabited: `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited());`. Correspondingly, DataflowConstProp refused to traverse a downcast into an uninhabited variant, returning `None` from its projection closure when `op.layout.for_variant(&self.ecx, idx).abi.is_uninhabited()`. In other words, the original logic assumed there is no valid MIR that downcasts to an uninhabited variant, and either skipped the projection (DataflowConstProp) or treated its occurrence as an internal compiler error (interpret projection).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is the rejection of a downcast-to-uninhabited-variant during const propagation: DataflowConstProp maps `TrackElem::Variant(idx)` to `None` whenever the target variant layout is uninhabited instead of performing `project_downcast`, and the const-eval projection layer backs this up with `assert!(!layout.abi.is_uninhabited())`. On input whose MIR contains a downcast to an uninhabited variant followed by a field read, this produces either missed propagation or an ICE, rather than allowing the projection and treating the uninhabited field value as uninitialized/arbitrary. The corrected transformation performs the downcast unconditionally (`TrackElem::Variant(idx) => self.ecx.project_downcast(op, idx).ok()`), and operand extraction maps an uninhabited field to `Immediate::Uninit`; GVN may consequently fold the field read to a constant such as `_1 = const 0_u32;`. The PR documents that the downcast itself is not UB: `This operation itself is never UB, all it does is change the type of the place.`
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing an enum whose variant is uninhabited, e.g. an enum like `E { A(!, u32) }` with `#![feature(never_type)]`, typically reached through a union or otherwise impossible construction, and a `Downcast` projection to that variant followed by a field projection/read. The supplied regression input is: a union `U { i: u32, e: E }`, and `let E::A(_, i) = unsafe { (&U { i: 0 }).e }; i` inside a const fn, compiled with `-O`; the const-eval UI test uses `let E::A(ref a) = unsafe { &(&U { u: () }).e };`. Two programs can differ only in whether DataflowConstProp performs the downcast-and-field projection or skips it because the variant is uninhabited.
analysis.summary: Confirmed bug fix for uninhabited-variant downcasts: DataflowConstProp must not skip a downcast merely because the target variant is uninhabited, and const-eval projection must not assert that the variant is inhabited. A downcast only changes the place type and is not itself UB; if a field's layout is uninhabited, const prop should forget the data (`Immediate::Uninit`) so GVN can fold the field read to a constant. The historical rejection caused an ICE and prevented valid optimization of MIR that can arise via unions/impossible enum values.
analysis.trigger: A `Downcast` projection whose target enum/coroutine variant has an uninhabited layout (for example a never-type field such as `A(!, u32)`), especially when reached through a union or other construction that makes the value impossible, and const propagation/GVN attempts to project or read a field of that variant.
preconditions: The enum has a variant containing an uninhabited type (requires `#![feature(never_type)]` in the regression tests).
MIR contains a downcast to that variant and a subsequent field read.
For the original Miri failure, validation is disabled in the test (`-Zmiri-disable-validation`) because validation otherwise stops before the ICE.
The GVN regression test uses `-O`, `// unit-test: GVN`, `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and `// skip-filecheck`.
pitfalls: Do not treat the downcast operation itself as UB: the patch changes the docs to say `This operation itself is never UB, all it does is change the type of the place.`
Do not assume `layout.abi.is_uninhabited()` implies the projection is unreachable in optimized MIR; the issue arose precisely because MIR can contain such a downcast.

The GVN diff shows `_1 = ((_2 as A).1: u32)` becoming `_1 = const 0_u32`; this arbitrary constant is acceptable only because constructing a value of the uninhabited variant is already impossible/UB. Do not generalize this to inhabited variants.
The guard in DataflowConstProp and the assertion in const-eval projection are two halves of the same bug; fixing only one leaves either missed propagation or an ICE.
The test file name/comment being retained is not evidence of the transformation; compare the actual assignments in the before/after MIR diffs.
The panic-abort and panic-unwind diff files have identical folded bodies here; do not infer a panic-strategy-specific difference from the file names alone.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a UI `// check-pass` test under `tests/ui/consts/` that evaluates a const with an uninhabited variant and a union, matching `let-irrefutable-pattern-ice-120337.rs`. Add a Miri pass test with `-Zmiri-disable-validation` for the runtime/interpretation path. Add a MIR opt test under `tests/mir-opt/` using `// unit-test: GVN`, `-O`, `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, and `EMIT_MIR gvn_uninhabited.f.GVN.diff`; assert GVN rewrites the downcast field read and subsequent assignment to `const 0_u32`. Run both panic strategies via the emitted diffs. Also exercise DataflowConstProp directly because the GVN test covers the shared const-prop projection path.
evidence: // This variant may in fact be uninhabited.
This operation itself is never UB, all it does is change the type of the place.
// If the field is uninhabited, we can forget the data (can happen in ConstProp).
`enum S { A(!), B, C }` is an example of an enum with Scalar layout that
has an `Uninhabited` variant, which means this case is possible.
